title: TechBus
subtitle: B2B IT marketplace - Team project
description: The IT industry is disconnected: businesses looking for IT services, vendors selling them, professionals, the recruiters who hire them and the training centers who teach them all work in separate silos. TechBus is a unified technology ecosystem that connects all of them through one intelligent network, bringing procurement, vendor discovery, talent acquisition, professional development and learning into a single connected experience.
role: Main front-end contributor on a small team. I built the majority of TechBus's React application across all five platforms, shipping most of the product's screens end to end, from first login to daily use.
highlights: Built most of the React front end for five connected platforms that serve businesses, vendors, IT professionals, recruiters and training centers.
Built the vendor and business quote marketplace, including quote comparison.
Built onboarding flows and dashboards for every user type.
Built billing and subscriptions.
Created a shared component system that kept five differently branded platforms visually consistent as the product grew.

title: ImperialJet
subtitle: Website redesign
description:
ImperialJet, a Munich-based private jet charter operator, had a slow WordPress website with a dated, hard-to-use interface. I rebuilt the front end in React to fix both: a quote request flow with airport search, service and safety pages, a fleet section with aircraft detail pages, and a contact page, in light and dark themes.

The redesign was cancelled before launch, so it was never deployed and there is no live link or public code. The screenshots show the finished front end. The forms use a mock submit because no backend was built, and the photography is free stock (Unsplash) standing in for the company’s own.
role: Front-end developer. I rebuilt the site end to end: information architecture, the design system, every page and component, the quote flow, and the performance and accessibility work.
highlights: Replaced the slow, dated WordPress front end with a React single-page app focused on speed, clarity and accessibility.
Built a three-step quote request flow (route, passengers, details) with per-field validation, focus management between steps, a review summary and a mocked submit.

Wrote an accessible airport search (ARIA combobox with full keyboard support) over 9,101 airports. The open dataset is converted to a compact JSON at build time and loaded only when a field is first used.
Created a design system with tokens for colour, type and spacing, with light and dark themes that follow the system setting, remember the choice and apply before first paint so there is no flash.
Replaced three copy-pasted content pages with one data-driven template (sticky in-page navigation, scroll-spy, fact callouts and a contextual call to action per section).
Built fleet pages with a lightbox photo viewer using the native dialog element, cabin layouts, a comparison table and a sticky mobile request bar.
Reached Lighthouse scores of 90-95 for performance (mobile, throttled) and 100 for accessibility, best practices and SEO on the production build.
Cut the main JavaScript bundle by 38% (155 to 96 kB gzipped) with route-level code splitting, lazy-loaded libraries and inline SVG icons, and reduced the hero image from 8.6 MB to 130 kB with WebP.
Verified the flows with a scripted browser test of 20 user journeys (search, multi-step form, theme, navigation, lightbox) and a check for horizontal overflow on phones.

title: Novagram
subtitle: Social media app
description: Novagram is an Instagram-style social media web app. The front end is built with React and the original backend with Flask and SQLAlchemy. The live demo runs on a built-in mock API, so you can register for an account, create a post and explore around without a server.
role: Full stack developer. I designed and built the React front end and the Flask + SQLAlchemy API, then added the mock API that powers the live demo.
highlights: Built a full social feed with likes, comments, saves, follows, notifications and search.
Managed server state with React Query: an infinite-scroll Explore feed, mutations for likes and follows, and targeted cache invalidation so only affected data refetches.
Designed a responsive UI in plain CSS, with a dedicated mobile navigation and a dark theme, and no CSS framework.
Originally built with a Flask + SQLAlchemy REST backend and cloud image uploads; the live demo runs on a mock API so it works without a server.
Built a reusable UI kit (dialogs with focus trapping, buttons, switches, skeletons) and a design-token system with light and dark themes.
Cut the initial JavaScript by 43% (149 to 85 kB gzipped) with route-level code-splitting and idle prefetching.

title: Ultimate Game Launcher
subtitle: PC game store and launcher
description:
A game launcher in the style of Steam and Epic. There's a store where you find and buy games, and a library where you install, update and play them. The 103 games in the catalog are real ones, pulled from Steam's public store pages along with their DLC, editions and age ratings.

Nothing is actually for sale. Accounts, purchases, downloads and friends are all simulated and saved in your browser, so there's no backend. Log in as the demo player and click around.
role: Solo project. I did the design and all of the code, including the scripts that import the catalog from Steam.
highlights: Wrote Node scripts that pull games, screenshots, DLC and ESRB/PEGI ratings from Steam's store API. That's how the catalog got to 103 games and 145 DLC without typing any of it in.
Browse filters (genre, player modes, price) live in the URL, so you can send someone a link to a filtered view.
Game pages are static and rebuild every hour. An upcoming game becomes playable on its release day without a redeploy.
Checkout handles editions, bundles, coupons, gifts and upgrading to a higher edition. Refunds use Steam's rule: under 2 hours played and within 14 days.
The downloads are fake, but the download manager works like a real one. You can reorder the queue, pause and resume, and watch the speed graph and time left.
You can add friends and message them. Demo players reply after a few seconds, and the reply depends on what you sent.
Download progress updates twice a second, so it has its own React context. In the main store it would re-render the whole app.
Passwords are stored as salted SHA-256 hashes, even though everything stays on your machine.
Pricing, refunds, coupons and release dates are covered by unit tests (Vitest).
